title: Inside your computer: running four lines of Java
intro: Let's look inside the machine while it runs a tiny program. First, a guess!

predict.question: Where does the text "Ilma" live while the program runs?
options: In the stack box called name
On the heap, with name pointing to it
predict.reveal: Text is an object, so it lives on the heap. The stack box called name only holds a reference to it.

takeaway: Primitives sit in stack boxes; objects live on the heap and the stack holds a reference to them.

steps.say: This is your computer. The CPU runs one line at a time and memory holds the values. Let's run four lines of Java.
int age = 17 makes a small box on the stack called age and drops 17 in it. Simple values live right there.
A String is an object, so the text goes on the heap. The stack box name only keeps a reference pointing to it.
Stack is small, fast and cleaned up automatically. Heap is roomier and holds objects. A reference is just an address linking the two.
age = age + 1: the CPU reads 17 from the box, adds 1, and writes 18 back into the same box.
println follows the reference name -> s1 to find the text, joins it with age, and sends the result to the console.
When main() ends its stack frame vanishes. Nothing points to the String any more, so the garbage collector may free it.
